title: Madeleines
description: Buttery French tea cakes with a delicate lemon perfume and the signature bump on top. The batter rests in the fridge before baking, which is the secret to that distinctive rise.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: 1 stick, melted and cooled, plus more for greasing

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and sugar together in a large bowl until pale and thick, about 2 minutes by hand or 1 minute with an electric mixer. The mixture should fall in thick ribbons when you lift the whisk.
steps.tip: Getting this mixture properly aerated is what gives madeleines their light, spongy texture. Don't rush it.

steps.text: Whisk in the honey, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt over the egg mixture. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined — no dry streaks, but don't overmix.
Drizzle in the melted butter and fold until the batter is smooth and glossy.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
steps.tip: Chilling firms the butter in the batter. When it hits the hot oven, the cold butter creates steam that pushes up the signature bump.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Brush a madeleine pan with melted butter and dust lightly with flour, tapping out the excess.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon of batter into each mold, filling them about three-quarters full. Don't spread the batter — it will flow into the shell shape on its own in the oven.
Bake until the edges are golden and the tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 10 to 12 minutes. The bump on top should be puffed and set.
Immediately unmold the madeleines onto a wire rack by tapping the pan firmly against the counter. Dust with powdered sugar while still warm.
